key_insight: Co-PiLOT turns inverse design into latent-space search, combining a generative decoder as a validity prior with physics-informed optimization to efficiently target desired material microstructures.
engineering_relevance: For materials engineers, this offers a practical path to optimize complex, non-Euclidean microstructures under expensive simulator constraints while preserving feasibility.
method: Train a ViT-based encoder on ~80k EBSD microstructure images to compress structures into a low-dimensional latent code.
Use latent diffusion / DiT / rectified-flow decoders to reconstruct high-fidelity microstructures and convert them to solver-ready grids via a self-segmenting orientation codec.
Run MERIDIAN latent optimization with uncertainty-aware GP models, feasibility prediction, trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On magnesium alloy microstructure/texture inverse design, the ViT-FMDiT decoder achieved the best reconstruction quality reported (FID 27.86, MS-SSIM 0.178), and the MERIDIAN + ViT-FMDiT setup reduced relative target error by 3–22% versus seven baselines within 160 simulations.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and domain coverage of the learned decoder; if the latent manifold misses rare but physically valid structures, the optimizer may converge to locally plausible but suboptimal designs.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
